subject: Post-demo: 3-week validation pilot — success metrics, owners, timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@arcadialabs.com>, Liam Park <liam.park@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: 3-week validation pilot — success metrics, owners, timeline

Hi Emma / Liam,

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation and really clear product fit around your agent-assist use case. As promised, I’ve sketched a focused 3-week validation pilot to demonstrate latency, cost per request, and end-to-end quality on your sample ticket dataset. The attached PDF (arcadia_pilot_outline.pdf) includes the detailed schedule and an acceptance checklist.

High-level summary:
- Goal: Validate that Redwood’s hosted inference reduces first-response time and improves suggested-reply quality by measured NPS uplift on a 3-week pilot.
- Success criteria (pass/fail checks):
  - Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 350ms on our config
  - Quality: Precision@3 of suggested replies >= 78% on your labeled eval set
  - Cost: < $0.015 per conversation on average (baseline provided in doc)
- Timeline: Week 0 (prep) → Weeks 1–3 (validation) → Week 4 (wrap + decision)
- Ownership:
  - Redwood: Ben Carter — integration & monitoring setup
  - Arcadia: Emma Jensen — data mapping & test labels
  - Redwood: Marissa Cole — success-metric validation and reporting

Requested next steps from your side:
1) Confirm the three success metrics above or propose edits by EOD Wed (Apr 25).
2) Provide a sample of ~2k anonymized ticket pairs (input + ideal reply) and the schema for the API keys/data access.
3) Approve the proposed canary window for Week 1 (we’ll keep traffic low and synthetic load to validate latency).

Attachments: arcadia_pilot_outline.pdf (detailed schedule + acceptance checklist).

If this looks good I’ll open a HubSpot task and create the shared Drive folder for artifacts — link in my follow-up.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | (650) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs

From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@arcadialabs.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 15:02:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: 3-week validation pilot — success metrics, owners, timeline

Soojin, thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear checklist. A couple quick clarifications before we sign off on the scope:

1) Data volume: The 2k ticket sample is fine for evaluation, but in Week 2 we expect to run against ~10k incoming messages (production-shaped traffic). Can Redwood provide guidance on how the cost/latency estimates scale to that volume?
2) Security: We need a SOC 2 snapshot and a short statement on data retention for the pilot (are logs stored? for how long?).
3) Canary: We prefer the canary to run with <5% of traffic to start, then increase to 20% after stability checks — is that supported?

If you can confirm these items and send the SOC 2 excerpt, we can move forward. Tentatively we’re good to start the prep week in the week beginning May 6, subject to legal/IT okaying the access.

Thanks — I’ll loop Liam here to keep him in the scheduling thread.

—Emma
Emma Jensen
Senior Product Manager, Arcadia Labs
emma.jensen@arcadialabs.com

Looping in a quick technical runbook and proposed cut-over plan. Emma — short answers to your questions:

- Scaling guidance: our estimate in the outline is conservative; at 10k requests/day we expect 95th pctl latency to stay within ~20–30% of the pilot numbers depending on batchability of your load. I put sample cost projections per 1k requests in the runbook.
- SOC2/data retention: attaching a SOC2 summary (soc2_report_stub.pdf) and the pilot retention policy: we keep logs for the pilot environment for 30 days by default; we can shorten on request and provide a deletion confirmation.
- Canary flow: yes — we support staged rollouts (5% → 20% → 100%). We’ll instrument tracing and a simple RTT/err rate guard to abort automatically if thresholds are breached.

Action items I’ll take on from Redwood:
- Ben: create integration checklist and short-run observability dashboard (deadline May 10)
- Marissa: define the evaluation sampling and scoring job (deadline May 17)

Attachments: quick_runbook.xlsx (integration checklist, sample kpis).

Ben

- SOC2: attaching stub (soc2_report_stub.pdf) — we’ll provide full SOC2 evidence to your security reviewer; pilot logs retention is 30 days and we’ll issue deletion evidence on completion.
- Canary: we’ll run 5% → 20% staged rollout with automated abort thresholds and observability hooks.

Schedule (dates tentative):
- Prep week: May 6–10 — data handoff, keys, runbook walk-through
- Week 1 (canary): May 13–19 — low traffic validation + latency checks
- Week 2: May 20–26 — increased traffic, scoring on 10k/day shape
- Week 3: May 27–31 — collection for final metrics and decision session the week of June 3

Owners & action items (owner — due):
- Emma Jensen — provide data sample and schema (May 3)
- Ben Carter — integration checklist & dashboard (May 10)
- Marissa Cole — final evaluation scoring job and baseline comparison (May 17)
- Soojin Lee — HubSpot task and shared Drive folder; coordinate legal (May 1)

Links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.company/deal/ARC-4721), shared Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cArcadiaPilot).

Next steps (from Redwood): I’ll open the Drive folder with the pilot artifacts, share the SOC2 excerpt with your security contact, and Ben will schedule the integration kickoff with your infra team. If legal needs a short MSA amendment for the pilot we can loop in engineering/legal ops — otherwise the existing terms will cover the 3-week eval.

Please reply-all to confirm the schedule and owners or propose changes. If I don’t hear by EOD Thu (Apr 27) I’ll assume May 6 prep week is acceptable and will proceed to create the HubSpot tasks.
